title: A Point-of-Prescription Safety-Check System for Adverse Drug Reactions in Rural Bangladeshi Hospitals: A Feasibility Study
abstract: arXiv:2608.27239v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Adverse drug reactions (ADRs) are a major, largely preventable source of patient harm. In high-income settings, electronic health records store a patient's allergy history and warn prescribers when a contraindicated drug is ordered; in rural Bangladeshi public hospitals no such record exists for outgoing patients, a single physician may see on the order of one patient per minute, and a patient's history of severe reactions does not survive between visits. This paper proposes and outlines the evaluation of a lightweight, smartphone-based safety-check system for this setting. At registration a soft identifier (a phone number) is recorded; after the physician writes a prescription, its image is captured, the brand names are resolved to active ingredients using national drug references, and the ingredients are matched against the patient's recorded severe reaction history. The system is retrieval-based rather than predictive, and is silent

translated_title: 孟加拉国农村医院处方点不良反应安全核查系统：可行性研究
translated_abstract: 不良反应（ADR）是导致患者伤害的主要且大多可预防的原因。在高收入环境中，电子健康记录存储患者的过敏史，并在开具禁忌药物时警告处方医生；而在孟加拉国农村公立医院，门诊患者没有此类记录，一位医生每分钟可能要看约一位患者，且患者严重不良反应的历史在就诊之间无法保留。本文提出并概述了一个针对该环境的轻量级、基于智能手机的安全核查系统的评估方案。在注册时记录一个软标识符（电话号码）；医生开具处方后，拍摄处方图像，利用国家药物参考将品牌名解析为活性成分，并将这些成分与患者记录的严重不良反应历史进行匹配。该系统基于检索而非预测，并且是静默的。
tldr: 本文提出了一种基于智能手机的轻量级安全核查系统，通过软标识符和处方图像识别，在孟加拉国农村医院中实现不良反应历史的实时匹配，以预防可避免的药物伤害。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a lightweight smartphone-based safety-check system that uses soft identifiers and prescription image recognition to match adverse drug reaction histories in real time, preventing avoidable medication harm in rural Bangladeshi hospitals.
